title: Throughput Audit Harness: statistically-driven prober and customer acceptance suite
creator: Jonah Park
description: Build a robust, statistical load-testing harness and customer acceptance suite that can certify Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees, validate autoscaling policy behavior under realistic waveforms, and produce reproducible customer-facing artifacts for acceptance. The harness should be able to run in our lab and in customer-like network/topology conditions, produce signed reports (CSV + HTML), and integrate with Console dashboards and rollouts for automated gating.
background: Current throughput validation tickets focus on synthetic peak runs and single-wave stress tests. Customers and Dedicated SLAs require documented steady-state throughput, latency SLOs under 99th-percentile conditions, and guarantees that autoscaling policies will not breach capacity windows. We need a single end-to-end harness that covers: 1) microbenchmarks (kernel-level), 2) mixed-workload customer simulations (chat + streaming + embeddings), and 3) acceptance templates that customers can run in their dedicated pools.
proposed_solution: Deliver a modular harness with three coordinated components: (A) load generator service (based on an extensible client derived from Locust + custom streaming driver) that supports synthetic and recorded workload replay, waveform scripting, KV-cache priming, and request-group correlation; (B) measurement engine that computes throughput, availability, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, per-model token/sec, and uses bootstrap resampling + change-point detection (CUSUM) to identify steady-state windows; (C) acceptance orchestrator that runs step-scaling experiments against autoscaling policies and fleet routing rules, produces pass/fail criteria, and uploads signed artifacts to the Console and s3. Key innovations: variance-aware step scaling (scale triggers only when confidence interval excludes threshold), steady-state detection to avoid warmup bias, and a customer-mode that replaces synthetic backends with opaque customer traffic capture replay. The harness will emit: signed HTML report, CSV of raw samples, PNG graphs, and a JSON summary compatible with Console ingestion. We will also provide a lightweight on-prem-mode script for customers to run in their VPC, which posts results to a pre-authorized endpoint for acceptance automation.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a mixed workload (chat: 60%, streaming: 20%, embedding: 20%) and produce a reproducible signed report
Steady-state detection implemented; throughput reported with 95% confidence intervals and p95/p99 latency metrics
Autoscaling policy probe runs: simulated step up and step down with asserted no more than 10% SLA breach during transient for P1 customers
Console integration: report uploaded and visible in per-customer rollout dashboard
Customer acceptance template and runbook published to Confluence and accessible from Support playbooks
Benchmark reproducibility: same run in lab vs CI within ±5% median throughput for stable models

notes: We should avoid long constant-rate run durations — prefer multiple short stepped runs with steady-state detection to get robust CI metrics
KV cache priming matters: for LLM workloads we must include priming phase that matches customer prompt prefix distribution
Network jitter modeling: include a jitter multiplier so we can simulate on-prem customers behind NATs and lossy links
We will initially support two driver modes: synthetic generator and recorded-replay (captured from prod traffic anonymized)
Trade-off: detailed GPU-level metrics require privileged exporters on Dedicated nodes — keep opt-in for customer-run scripts
